topic_relevance.J04: adjacent（限方法背景）：文章明确构造补偿 Poisson 随机测度驱动的非负跳 SDE，并在可积性条件下使用跳积分鞅和 Itô 公式；但目标是遍历性/收敛率，未给随机 Fubini 交换定理、退出停时的财富结算，亦未把补偿项结成目标接口。不能作为 J04 目标结论的直接证据。

definitions.name: Wasserstein contraction
definitions.statement: W1 使用代价 |x−y| 的最优耦合距离；证明基于同噪声耦合和过程次序比较。

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2: order comparison and W1 exponential contraction
assumptions: Nonnegative strong jump SDE (3.1), admissible drift/diffusion/jump coefficients and local Osgood-type conditions (3.a)–(3.c), ensuring existence, uniqueness and pathwise comparison.
(3.d): the combined compensated Gaussian and compensated-jump stochastic integral M_t is a martingale.
(3.e): for some A>0, b̄(y)−b̄(x)≤−A(y−x) whenever 0≤x≤y. Initial laws have finite first moment.
theorem_cards.statement: Proposition 3.1 gives unique strong nonnegative solutions and order preservation. Under (3.a)–(3.e), Theorem 3.2 gives W1(P_t^*μ,P_t^*ν)≤e^{−At}W1(μ,ν), a unique invariant law π∈P1, and the same exponential contraction toward π.
proof_steps: Couple solutions from x≤y using the same noises; pathwise order gives |X_t^y−X_t^x|=X_t^y−X_t^x.
Taking expectations in the SDE removes the martingale term under (3.d), yielding E|X_t^y−X_t^x|=y−x+∫_0^t E[b̄(X_s^y)−b̄(X_s^x)]ds.
Apply (3.e) and Gronwall to obtain E|X_t^y−X_t^x|≤|y−x|e^{−At}.
Use the joint-law coupling for point masses, convexity of W1, and an optimal coupling of arbitrary initial laws to get contraction.

Iterates under the semigroup are Cauchy in complete P1, giving an invariant law; contraction establishes convergence. Uniqueness among all invariant laws is shown with bounded cost 1∧|x−y| and dominated convergence.
gaps: Existence/comparison for the SDE is summarized from Dawson–Li [10], not reproved in this article.
The paper assumes (3.d); it does not give a general stochastic-Fubini theorem establishing it.
Its stopping/localization arguments in Sections 4–5 serve moment estimates and Lyapunov bounds, not an exit-time account/settlement identity.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 5.7: total variation convergence for subcritical CBI processes
assumptions: Admissible CBI parameters with b>0; immigration log-moment condition (1.5); Grey condition (5.a).
π is the unique invariant distribution; initial law belongs to P_log.
theorem_cards.statement: There is C>0 such that transition kernels satisfy ||P_t(x,·)−P_t(y,·)||_TV≤C min{1,e^{−bt}|x−y|}, and ||P_t^*μ−π||_TV≤C min{e^{−bt},W_log(μ,π)}+Ce^{−bt}W_log(μ,π).
proof_steps: Factor each CBI transition law into a no-immigration branching law and an immigration convolution; use translation/convolution contraction and the cited Theorem 5.6 for the branching kernel.
Integrate the pointwise total-variation estimate over an optimal coupling and apply convexity of Wasserstein distance.
Convert min{1,e^{−bt}|x−y|} to a logarithmic cost, then use the elementary log inequality from (5.11) and Theorem 5.5.
gaps: The estimate relies on the prior Li–Ma Theorem 5.6 and affine-process result Theorem 5.5; this theorem is unrelated to the requested jump-settlement interface.

constant_dependence.explicit: The Wasserstein contraction rate A is the effective drift dissipation constant from (3.e); CBI rates use b>0 and unspecified finite constants C. Martingale integrability is an assumption, not a derived universal constant.

endpoint_limits.scope: Nonnegative jump SDEs with pathwise comparison and dissipative effective drift; selected CBI/CNBI/CBIRE examples.
endpoint_limits.not_established: No stochastic Fubini theorem for interchanging time and jump integration, no optional-stopping exit settlement identity, no wealth/claim balance at a stopping boundary.

reusable_methods.method: Separate the compensated small-jump martingale from the uncompensated integrable jump drift, and formulate explicitly the required martingale condition.
reusable_methods.transfer: This can inform an interface audit for compensation bookkeeping; the article does not prove the target random-Fubini or stopping-boundary equality.

reusable_methods.method: Use same-noise order-preserving coupling, take expectations after verifying the martingale term, then apply effective-drift dissipativity and Gronwall.
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires the scalar nonnegative comparison structure and contractive drift; not applicable to arbitrary marked jump systems without those hypotheses.

reusable_methods.method: For CBI kernels, factor a transition law into branching and immigration convolution, then exploit convolution contraction.
reusable_methods.transfer: This is a semigroup decomposition for a specific branching model; not a general exit-time decomposition.

unchecked: All 23 PDF pages including the appendix were read; background existence/comparison results and Theorem 5.6 are cited rather than independently reproved.
